chapter: Cabarets and the Red Light District
title: Tonks and barrelhouses: drinks and the back dance room
summary: Prices of whiskey, beer and Angelica wine, what barrelhouses and tonks looked like, and the piano in the back room.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Well it's not a, you couldn't say it's a 12 bar blues because they'll all make 20 bars and they'll say this. I see. And it's just very slow, you walk into that same temple all night long. And the places they call tunks. Now a tunk, you'll know you won't know what a tunk is. A tunk is where sometimes you have a piano playing in there and they're serving whiskey and everything else in this place. Say you get a glass of whiskey, a glass of beer was like this for a nickel. You can get from a nickel drink, the highest drink they had in those tunk was 15 cents. That's your best whiskey, 15 cents. Whiskey. For a glass of it? Yeah, for a little. For a glass. A glass is bigger than with redoxin and you had a glass of whiskey. Just like a glass of beer was like this for a nickel. So you pay it. For a pint of whiskey it wasn't more than 50 cents. See, you didn't have nothing but points. But you could go to a barrel house and buy a nickel worth of second best whiskey, the barrel whiskey. The barrel house, I don't know if you've ever seen what you call a barrel house, it's a big bar and it's got barrels sitting on racks all around, you know, around the wall, see. Oh yeah? Yeah, all around the wall. You go in there and get second best whiskey. Well you go to either one of those boughs and get you a second best whiskey. They had another drink they used to call Angelica. That's what it's called. What was it called? Angelica. See, now you get a cup like this for a nickel, see. Not for a dime, a big cup like that. Now you drink one of those cups, you got enough to lash it. What was that? Angelica. It's, it tastes like sherry wine but it wasn't sherry wine, and that's the sherry wine, see. That's what it's called, the sheep girl's sherry wine. Now your best sherry wine was that was twenty-five cents a quart back in the day. What did those tonks look like? Well tonks, they're just a, they're just a old saloon like in the front, they got a big room in the back with a piano in it, no chairs. On his chair in there they go with the piano sitting on. See. And they get in there and dance and they leave them dancing and go to the bar like this, the trunk here, the back here, well this would be the front that's the bar in there. The bar, there wouldn't be no big bar, it'd be about lungs as big, there's nothing to, see. Well the baby roger that guy had to get the best piano player, the guy who played the best blues, he had to make his crowd back in the day, see. That's what the trunk looked like. There's some big, what do you call it, funky room. Not clean, but dirty. They go in there with all the walls on and everything. Go anyway. When people went there did they take their own girls with them or did they have girls in those places? No, no, no. See back in those days, cabarets, you never take no girls to cabarets. They always had the girls. You ever went to one of those jitney dances where the girls stand in the middle of the floor wait for you to come and ask them to buy tickets?
